speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness. To better understand your condition, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the combination of fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, and your recent release from prison raises concern for tuberculosis or other chronic infections. Have you had any close contacts with active tuberculosis or been exposed to anyone with a similar illness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Tuberculosis. The clinical presentation of chronic cough, fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, and generalized weakness over six months, combined with a high-risk social history of recent prison release, is highly suggestive of active tuberculosis. Immediate isolation and initiation of anti-tubercular therapy are indicated while awaiting confirmation.
